newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Southeast power prices up ahead of holiday.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Southeast power prices up ahead of holiday.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the U.S. Southeast were mostly higher Tuesday in thin trade, as sources said they anticipated a larger industrial demand following the holiday.

Firm, peak power prices in the northern part of the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) territory for Thursday were assessed in the $14.00-15.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) range, as compared with Monday's range of $11.00-12.00.
Firm, off-peak electricity in northern TVA was notionally assessed in the $10.00-12.00 area.
At the Georgia/Florida border, prices for firm, peak electricity in 16 hour blocks for Thursday delivery were talked in the $20.00-21.00 range, steady to up from Monday's $18.50-20.00 trading range.
Firm, off-peak power for Thursday at the Ga./Fla. border was notionally around $11.00.
In Florida, where temperature highs are in the 70s and 80s Fahrenheit and lows are in the 50s and 60s, firm, peak power prices on a 16-hour schedule were mostly steady in the $21.00-22.00 area.
Temperatures in the Southeast are expected to remain at least 10-20 degrees above-normal through the end of the week amid isolated thunderstorms hit the region.
Separately, Duke Power said the 1,129 megawatt Catawba 1 nuclear unit in South Carolina, shut Monday due to a relay failure, would likely restart Tuesday morning.
